statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Nasdaq-100 conditions remain orderly and two-sided, with NQ back near the session high in a narrow range about two hours before the US August employment report at 12:30 UTC.
recommendation: The assessment favours a narrow evidence-based danger window covering the payrolls release and the first hour of US cash trade rather than a session-wide restriction. Tail remains below the block threshold on currently observed evidence, and the CME weekend closure from 21:00 UTC removes live price-path exposure for the final thirteen hours of the forecast window.
headline: NQ recovers to within 12 points of the 29,673.00 session high in a 0.65% range as VIX holds 14.21 into the August payrolls report
body: NQ futures trade at 29,660.75, about +0.46% against a 29,524.75 prior settlement, inside an overnight range of 29,482.00 to 29,673.00 that spans roughly 0.65%. An independent quote source shows 29,662.00 with the identical 29,673.00 high. Price sits about 12 points below that high after the roughly 42-point pullback observed an hour earlier was recovered, so the market is holding near the session extreme, but the retracement did occur and was orderly, and total directional efficiency across the overnight remains low. Cross-asset alignment is weak: S&P 500 E-minis were roughly flat and Dow E-minis slightly negative alongside the Nasdaq-led move, which points to narrow index leadership rather than a broad one-way regime. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed Sep 3 at 29,482.32, up 1.16% in a 29,160.96 to 29,538.76 range, after Fed Governor Christopher Waller said he would be inclined to hold rates steady if inflation pressures continue to ease; that cut September hike odds to about 50.4% from 63.2% and pulled the 10-year yield toward 4.75%, against the 4.79% H.15 print for Sep 2, with the 2-year at 4.39%. VIX at 14.21 is down 0.77% in a 14.13 to 14.25 range, consistent with a market that is not pricing a violent payrolls reaction. WTI at $90.71 is down 0.64% on the day but up roughly 9% on the week on continued Strait of Hormuz disruption, with Brent at $95.28; that supply premium is a persistent backdrop rather than a fresh escalation at the cutoff. Delayed latest-session context shows semiconductors uniformly bid and megacap performance mixed, which supports the narrow-leadership reading. The August employment report is expected to show roughly +53,000 to +56,000 payrolls with unemployment at 4.1% after July's -23,000; because the debate is about a September hike rather than a cut, a strong print is the hawkish outcome and repricing risk is genuinely two-sided. Tail remains below the block threshold because no persistent no-retracement structure, failed retracement sequence, or aligned cross-asset amplifier has been observed; event importance and forecast dispersion are carried in Stress and Confidence instead.

lookbackSummary: The past 24 hours are fully covered by published Claude assessments. The Sep 3 European session was benign with Tail near 13 to 14 and the mode assessed as normal. The mode shifted to trend-up across the US cash session as the Waller-driven rally developed, with Tail peaking at 21 and Stress at 62, then decayed through the US evening as the move matured and the cash index closed up 1.16%. Overnight into Sep 4 the mode returned to normal, Tail held a tight 12 to 16 band and Stress eased into the low 50s before climbing steadily back to 59 as the payrolls report drew closer. No hour in the window produced a persistent no-retracement path, and the highest published Tail stayed below the block threshold throughout.
outlookSummary: The baseline holds a low-amplitude range through the remainder of the European session, with Stress building mechanically into the 12:30 UTC August employment report. The release hour and the following digestion hour, which contains the 13:30 UTC cash open, carry the widest two-sided repricing risk and are modelled at Tail 20 and 23, which map to WATCH rather than to a block. That is consistent with treating event importance and forecast dispersion as Stress and Confidence inputs until persistent one-way structure is actually observed, and with a genuinely two-sided rate distribution in which a strong print is the hawkish outcome. Tail is modelled to fall back below 20 from 15:00 UTC on the baseline that post-event discovery is orderly, with a modest tick up into the power hour for position squaring. From 21:00 UTC the CME weekend break removes live price discovery entirely, so the final thirteen slots carry a closed-market floor in which a mean-reversion failure has no venue in which to occur, and residual Stress there represents only weekend headline and gap risk expressible at the Sunday reopen.
